messages:
kevin-customer: Heads up — Acme (customer) reported a surge in token usage and a spike in API errors right after upgrading to redwood-python 1.12. They see a lot of 401s then repeated retries that blow up their billing. Minimal repro attached.

sara-support: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal repro + the exact pip/lockfile versions they used? Also which config flags they set on the client.

kevin-customer: Repro (from customer):

```python
# requirements.txt
# redwood==1.12.0

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="sk-XXX")
resp = client.generate("hello")
print(resp)
```

Logs: `AuthError: invalid token` then a flood of: `Retrying request (attempt 1)`, `Retrying request (attempt 2)` etc. They say previously (1.11.x) the client failed fast on 401 but after 1.12 it keeps retrying until account hits quota.

sara-support: Thanks. @julia-sdk can you weigh in — did anything change around default retry behavior or auth handling in 1.12?

julia-sdk: Yes — we removed the old `max_retries` parameter and replaced with a new `retry_policy` object to support backoff strategies. Unfortunately we missed a compatibility shim: if callers pass legacy keywords (or omit explicit policy) some code paths now fall back to the new default which is more aggressive and occasionally retries on 401s during transient auth errors. That explains the customer symptoms.

mike-eng: Repro confirmed locally: with redwood==1.12.0, a transient 401 triggers up to 10 retries (exponential) before surfacing. With 1.11.7 the client returned the 401 immediately.

julia-sdk: Short-term mitigations: 1) ask customer to pin to 1.11.7 or 1.11.x until we ship a patch; 2) they can set the env var `REDWOOD_RETRY_STRATEGY=none` or explicitly pass `retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=0)` in the client constructor to disable retries. Example: 

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient, RetryPolicy
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="sk-XXX", retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=0))
# OR export REDWOOD_RETRY_STRATEGY=none in their runtime
```

sara-support: Can you draft a short message we can send the customer with steps + a pin recommendation and an apology? Also we should offer a billing credit for the excess tokens.

kevin-customer: I'll need the exact pip command to force the pin and the suggested patch ETA so they know if this is temporary.

julia-sdk: Pip pin command: `pip install redwood==1.11.7` or add `redwood==1.11.7` to requirements/poetry.lock. Patch plan: open PR with compatibility shim to respect legacy args and default to conservative retry-on-5xx-only behavior. Target: backport hotfix to 1.12.1 within 48 hours. I'll open the PR now (WIP).

mike-eng: For customer transparency, repro curl that reproduces the retry behavior (they have a staging token you can use):

```bash
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# Server returns 401 once, client retries automatically multiple times
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-staging" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

nina-ops: deploy-bot just reported a regression alert for sdk-compat in monitoring: `sdk-retry-regression-210345` — tagging oncall.

deploy-bot: [alert] sdk-retry-regression-210345 created by monitoring (high error rate for client 1.12.0).

julia-sdk: I've created PR #8423 with the shim + unit test and requested a fast-track review. If approved, we'll cut 1.12.1 with the conservative default and publish release notes calling out the change and the pin guidance.

sara-support: Great. Action items for support: 1) send customer pin + workaround + ETA (use text below), 2) offer token credit for the spike, 3) keep thread updated when 1.12.1 is published.

Suggested customer note (editable):

"Hi — we tracked this to a change in the Python SDK's retry defaults in 1.12.0 that can cause retries on auth failures in some edge cases. Short-term options: 1) pin to redwood==1.11.7 (pip install redwood==1.11.7) or 2) disable retries by setting env var `REDWOOD_RETRY_STRATEGY=none` or constructing the client with `retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=0)`. We will ship a patch (1.12.1) within ~48 hours that restores the conservative default. We're also happy to offer a credit for any excess usage caused by this regression. Apologies for the disruption — please let us know if you'd like us to patch your environment or confirm when you have the pin applied."

kevin-customer: I'll send that and ask if they want the credit. Thanks — keep me posted on the PR + release.

julia-sdk: Will do. I'll post the merge + PyPI release link here once available.

sara-support: Marking this as high priority and logging CSR for billing credit.

kevin-customer: Thanks everyone :pray:
